♰ 🇵🇭 9.6 MILLION Faithful at Record 31 Hour Procession of the Black Nazarene 🇵🇭 ♰

🎥 The 2026 Black Nazarene Traslación in Manila, Philippines 🇵🇭, concluded on January 10 after a record-breaking 30 hours and 50 minutes, marking the longest procession in the event's history. The annual religious event, held on January 9, drew an estimated 9.6 million devotees, making it one of the largest Catholic gatherings in the world. The procession began at Quirino Grandstand and traversed central Manila, with the image of the Black Nazarene—dating back to the 17th century—returning to Quiapo Church. 

The statue, believed to have been brought from Mexico in 1606 by Augustinian Recollect missionaries, is said to have turned black after surviving a ship fire during its voyage—an event interpreted as a miracle that deepened its spiritual significance. 

The devotion centers on the Black Nazarene, a life-size, ebony statue of Jesus carrying a cross, which is enshrined at the Minor Basilica and National Shrine of Jesus Nazareno (Quiapo Church). Millions of barefoot devotees participate in the procession, walking miles through Manila’s streets to touch the statue or pull its carriage, seeking healing, miracles, and spiritual renewal. The event includes a nine-day novena, multiple Masses.
